recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It preserves the applied resolution while removing a current-code ambiguity; no further FHIR-core source work is needed unless the work group wants a new standalone requirements-kind example separate from the later terminology-server example.
issue_request: FHIR-16115 was a Published FHIR-core Conformance change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking what it means when a CapabilityStatement used to define expectations lacks the capabilitystatement-expectation extension. The approved resolution was to add guidance that requirement-style CapabilityStatements list potentially relevant capabilities and rely on documentation or the existing extension to state the degree of expectation, plus an example using the extension.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by git-svn commit fd720e51a17d9ec14fd784c730cd97810dfd9ad1 / SVN revision 14436, which added the requested paragraph to source/capabilitystatement/capabilitystatement-introduction.xml and added capabilitystatement-expectation extension uses to the terminology-server CapabilityStatement example. A later link-maintenance commit updated the extension link to use [%extensions-location%].
additional_context: CapabilityStatement is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current CapabilityStatement.kind code system uses requirements, not requirement. FHIR-24698 later rewrote the terminology-server CapabilityStatement as an instance-kind terminology-service example while preserving expectation extension uses, so reverting that example to requirements-kind would conflict with later published work. The capabilitystatement-expectation StructureDefinition now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack and is linked from core through [%extensions-location%]. Zulip discussion confirms the original question was about communicating expectation levels for desired-system CapabilityStatements, and Confluence searches found no conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: Changed the existing FHIR-16115 paragraph from type "requirement" to kind requirements, aligning the guidance with the current conformance code. No new example was added because the active terminology-server example still demonstrates the expectation extension and its current instance kind is governed by FHIR-24698.
source_changes: source/capabilitystatement/capabilitystatement-introduction.xml: changed the FHIR-16115 guidance to refer to CapabilityStatements of kind requirements instead of type "requirement".
